summary: Market sentiment is cautiously risk-off as an ongoing US-Iran war continues to dominate macro conditions, disrupting global energy supply chains, straining European gas markets, and pushing British energy prices up 4%, while Iran-Oman diplomatic talks over Hormuz revenue-sharing offer a slim but closely watched de-escalation signal. The conflict is the primary macro driver, having stranded Qatari gas shipments for six months, boosted US LNG sales, and accelerated European and Asian investment in renewables as governments seek long-term energy independence. On the equity side, Okta surged 15% after beating estimates on AI-driven identity security demand, while Boston Scientific shares fell following a cyberattack disclosure, and markets are bracing for high-stakes earnings from Nvidia, CrowdStrike, and Salesforce, whose results could set the tone for the broader tech sector. The main risk factors investors are tracking include Iran-linked cyberattacks—highlighted by an FBI-scrutinized hack of a water sector supplier—geopolitical escalation around the Strait of Hormuz, persistent energy-cost inflation, and uncertainty around Federal Reserve policy, with economists pressing potential Fed Chair candidate Warsh to clarify his economic views ahead of Jackson Hole. In the short term, markets are likely to remain volatile and directionally dependent on the Nvidia, CrowdStrike, and Salesforce earnings prints, any shift in Iran-Oman negotiations, and incoming US inflation data, with energy-exposed European equities particularly vulnerable to further geopolitical deterioration.
